problem_context: Current generative modeling approaches face fundamental challenges in mapping from one distribution to another efficiently. While discriminative models simply map individual samples to labels, generative models must learn mappings between entire distributions - a significantly more complex task. Existing methods often require iterative procedures at inference time, performing multiple network evaluations to progressively transform samples from noise to data. This creates a trade-off between generation quality and computational efficiency. There is a need for generative models that can produce high-quality samples in a single forward pass, without sacrificing the modeling capacity that makes iterative methods successful. The challenge is to find a training paradigm that can learn complex distribution mappings without requiring iterative refinement during generation. A key insight is that the training process itself is inherently iterative - perhaps this iterative nature could be leveraged differently than current approaches.
desirable_properties: Should generate high-quality samples in a single forward pass
Should be trainable from scratch without requiring pre-trained models
Should scale effectively to high-resolution data
Should avoid mode collapse and capture the full data distribution
Should support conditional generation with flexible conditioning
Should work across different data modalities beyond just images
Should have a principled training objective that converges reliably
Should leverage the inherent iterative nature of neural network training in a novel way
Should define some form of equilibrium condition that indicates when the model has converged
field_context: Generative modeling is a fundamental problem in machine learning that aims to learn the underlying distribution of data and generate new samples from it. This field has seen rapid progress with various paradigms including adversarial training, variational approaches, and iterative refinement methods, each with their own trade-offs between sample quality, training stability, and inference efficiency. Most approaches focus on the inference-time computation, but the training process itself involves iterative updates that evolve the model's behavior over time.
